ambassador noun

also envoy, diplomat, emissary

classical

Liv. 21.30.8
Traupman 163, 176, 271

M-O s.v. diplomat

lēgātus, lēgātī m.

noun, second declension · Declension on Wiktionary

an ambassador, an envoy

One sent with a commission (lēgāre); also a general’s or a governor’s deputy (Lewis & Short). Traupman and Levi–Bini give it for an ambassador, Morgan–Owens for any diplomat.

Other words

  • ōrātor, ōrātōris m. — an envoy who speaks for his people

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Liv. 1.15.5: Vejentēs pācem petītum ōrātōrēs Rōmam mittunt; M-O s.v. diplomat: ambassador · Declension on Wiktionary

    The spokesman of an embassy (Lewis & Short); in Renaissance and modern Latin the usual title of an ambassador (Busbecq, Milton and Egger, in Morgan–Owens).

Examples

  • eōs ipsōs quōs cernant lēgātōs nōn pinnīs sublīme ēlātōs Alpēs trānsgressōs

    the very envoys they could see had not crossed the Alps lifted up on wingsLiv. 21.30.8

See also embassy, consul.
